newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on India export hopes.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on India export hopes.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on news India would import two million tonnes of wheat over the near term, traders said.
"The India news is adding a little more support to the market," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

India's Food Minister Devendra Prasad Yadav said Thursday India will import two million tonnes of wheat in fiscal 1996-97 (April-March) to augment domestic supplies and check rising prices. "The government has decided during the current financial year it will import two million tonnes of wheat," Yadav told the Indian parliament.
Rumors circulated early Thursday that India this week purchased one million tonnes of wheat from Australia.

Wheat futures also found support from USDA's weekly export sales report Thursday which showed U.S. net exports of wheat during the week ended December 5 at 346,200 tonnes. The market was expecting from 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes.
Prices also were boosted by USDA's minor upward adjustment in world ending wheat stocks for 1996-97 of 530,000 tonnes. There were expectations for a one- to two-million-tonne hike.
Wheat closed 3-1/2 to 6-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with December up five at $4.04.
Some traders early Thursday cited possible sales of wheat to Russia as supportive to wheat futures this week.
After Thursday's close there was news USDA had raised the GSM-102 credit line to Russia to $50 million from the previous $20 million for fiscal year 1997.
But skepticism remains that Russia will be a significant player in the wheat market.

"The former Soviet Union is no longer a factor in the world wheat market...it's not a player...they've got to have money to buy," said Gregg Doud of the U.S. Wheat Associates at a briefing Wednesday on the world wheat outlook.

Commercials were on both sides of the market Thursday with Continental Grain buying two million bushels of March and Cargill Inc bought two million July, traders said. O'Connor and Co bought two million March and Term Commodities, the marketing arm for Louis Dreyfus Corp sold five million bushels of March, traders said. FIMAT Futures sold three million bushels of March, they said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, above the 14,829 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, below the 8,720 traded Wednesday.
In wheat options, Smith Barney bought 800 March $4.00 calls at 3/4 cent and bought 400 July $3.30 puts at 18-1/2 cents, traders said.
